name: Heleb
overview: Heleb is a male figure identified as the son of Baanah and recognized as the sixteenth member among "the thirty," a distinguished group of David's mighty men. His tribal affiliation and additional personal details are not specified in Scripture. Heleb's role is noted primarily for his inclusion in this elite band of warriors serving King David.
namesAndTitles: The name Heleb appears in 2 Samuel 23:29 without an explicit meaning provided. A variant of his name, Heled, is found in 1 Chronicles 11:30 and is understood to mean "mole" in Hebrew. These names are proper names and were not given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Heleb is the son of Baanah, as noted in 2 Samuel 23:29. Beyond this paternal relationship, no further family connections are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Heleb's significance lies in his membership among "the thirty," a select group of David's mighty men known for their valor and loyalty. Being the sixteenth listed among these warriors highlights his role in the military strength supporting David's reign. His mention underscores the importance of faithful service in God's providential plan for Israel under David's kingship.
